propositions: git fetch to the GitHub mirror intermittently hangs beyond 300s timeout due to missing http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime configuration, allowing byte-starved connections to block indefinitely.

Adding http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 and http.lowSpeedTime=10 to git config enables throughput-keyed abort that terminates stalled fetches in ~10 seconds while allowing legitimately slow but progressing transfers to complete.
In-process retry of fetch on low-speed abort (bounded attempts) enables transient stalls to self-heal within the same review instead of deferring to backfill, reducing worst-case from 300s to ~30s.
Git subprocess and fetch-locking cluster is extracted from repo_snapshot.py into new git_fetch.py module to remain within 800 LOC module-size cap, with one-directional dependency.
